article_title: Leading doctor rebukes NHS chiefs over transplant crisis

tasks.prompt: What is the main issue raised in the article?
options: Britain has decided to end all organ transplants
A senior transplant doctor says NHS leaders have failed to solve workforce and capacity problems that delay or cancel transplants
Hospitals have too many specialist transplant staff
The NHS plans to replace donated organs with artificial ones immediately
tasks.correct_answer: A senior transplant doctor says NHS leaders have failed to solve workforce and capacity problems that delay or cancel transplants
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה מתמקדת בביקורת של רופא בכיר על כך שבעיות כוח אדם וקיבולת אינן מטופלות, ולכן השתלות מתעכבות או מתבטלות.

tasks.prompt: Who made the criticism described in the leaked letter?
options: A private insurance executive
A patient waiting for a routine appointment
Professor Derek Manas, medical director for organ donation and transplantation at NHS Blood and Transplant
The owner of a pharmaceutical company
tasks.correct_answer: Professor Derek Manas, medical director for organ donation and transplantation at NHS Blood and Transplant
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הביקורת נכתבה בידי פרופ' דרק מאנאס, המנהל הרפואי לתרומת איברים ולהשתלות ב־NHS Blood and Transplant.

tasks.prompt: What does “overhaul” mean when the article discusses the transplant system?
options: A minor change to one appointment
A temporary pause in surgery
A complete review and major reorganisation
A new type of donated organ
tasks.correct_answer: A complete review and major reorganisation
tasks.explanation_hebrew: overhaul פירושו בדיקה ושינוי יסודיים של מערכת, ולא תיקון קטן בלבד.

tasks.prompt: Why can a transplant be cancelled even after a donated organ becomes available?
options: The hospital may lack the staff, theatre or intensive-care capacity needed at short notice
The recipient must wait until the next calendar year
Donated organs can be used only during office hours
Every transplant requires approval from a private insurer
tasks.correct_answer: The hospital may lack the staff, theatre or intensive-care capacity needed at short notice
tasks.explanation_hebrew: זמינות איבר אינה מספיקה: נדרשים בזמן קצר צוות מיומן, חדר ניתוח ומקום בטיפול נמרץ, ולעיתים הקיבולת חסרה.

tasks.prompt: Why is transplantation especially difficult to manage with a limited workforce?
options: Transplant operations never need specialist staff
The timing and availability of donated organs are unpredictable, so teams must be ready at short notice
All organs arrive at the same planned time each week
Transplant staff work only with living donors
tasks.correct_answer: The timing and availability of donated organs are unpredictable, so teams must be ready at short notice
tasks.explanation_hebrew: מאחר שאי אפשר לתזמן מראש מתי איבר מתאים יגיע, המערכת זקוקה לכוח אדם ולקיבולת גמישים בכל שעה.

tasks.prompt: What does “fragmented” mean when describing transplant services?
options: Broken into separate parts that do not work together well
Fully staffed and centrally coordinated
Limited only to kidney operations
Recently funded with new equipment
tasks.correct_answer: Broken into separate parts that do not work together well
tasks.explanation_hebrew: fragmented מתאר שירות המחולק לגופים או חלקים שאינם מתואמים היטב.

tasks.prompt: Give three system problems identified in the article or the review it discusses.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין שלוש בעיות מערכתיות מדויקות ולא רק לומר שקיימת 'משבר'.
expected_points: An inadequate specialist workforce and difficult recruitment
Mismatch between unpredictable organ availability and hospital resources

tasks.prompt: Summarise the doctor's criticism, its consequences for patients and the changes being requested.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: הסיכום צריך לכלול את מקור הביקורת, בעיות הקיבולת וכוח האדם, הפגיעה בממתינים והצורך ברפורמה מתואמת.
expected_points: Professor Manas rebuked NHS leaders in a leaked letter
Workforce and capacity shortages can waste opportunities for transplant surgery
Patients face longer, unequal waits and last-minute cancellations
The system needs clearer accountability, planning and investment

tasks.prompt: Why is relying on staff goodwill not a sustainable way to run transplant services?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר שעבודה בלתי צפויה ואינטנסיבית דורשת תקנים, תכנון ומשאבים קבועים ולא מאמץ חריג ומתמשך של עובדים.
expected_points: Transplants may be required at any hour and at short notice
Repeated extra effort can exhaust staff and harm retention
Goodwill cannot create theatre beds or intensive-care capacity
Stable staffing, recruitment and funded rotas are needed for a reliable service

tasks.prompt: Propose a practical NHS response to the transplant-capacity crisis, using evidence from the article.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציע תוכנית הכוללת לפחות שני צעדים, להסביר כיצד הם מטפלים בבעיה, ולהתייחס לאחריות מערכתית.
expected_points: Recruit and retain specialist transplant staff
Protect flexible theatre and intensive-care capacity for unpredictable organ offers
Assign clear national responsibility and accountability
Measure cancellations and waiting-list outcomes to guide investment
